title: Which {que} - When the Next Verb Changes
description: Gather the phrases that change the verb after {que}, and the ones that leave it as it is.
can_do: Change the verb after a wish, a need or a feeling: {je veux que tu viennes}.
Keep the verb as it is after {je pense que}, and change it after {je ne pense pas que}.
line: After most phrases of wish, need, feeling or doubt, the verb after {que} takes the subjunctive: {il faut que tu partes}.

parts.heading: A special form after {que}
text: After some phrases with {que}, the next verb takes a special form called the subjunctive: {tu partes} in place of {tu pars}. After other phrases, the verb stays as it is.

rows.fr: je suis content que tu sois là

parts.heading: A wish, a need, a feeling
text: When you say what you want, what someone needs to do or how you feel about it, the verb after {que} usually changes.

blocks.heading: A wish or a need
lines: Il faut que tu fasses attention.
You need to pay attention.
Je veux que tu comprennes.
I want you to understand.
J'aimerais que tu sois là.
I'd like you to be there.

blocks.heading: A feeling
lines: Je suis triste que tu partes.
I'm sad you're leaving.
J'ai peur qu'il parte.
I'm afraid he'll leave.
Je regrette que tu ne puisses pas venir.
I'm sorry you can't come.

parts.heading: Belief or doubt
text: {je pense que} states what you believe, so the verb stays as it is. With {ne … pas}, it expresses a doubt, and the verb usually changes. {il est possible que} changes it too, but {peut-être que} keeps the verb as it is.

rows.fr: je ne pense pas qu'il vienne

lines: Je doute que ce soit possible.
I doubt that's possible.
Je ne crois pas qu'il ait raison.
I don't think he's right.

parts.heading: {avant que}, {pour que}, {bien que}
text: These three join two ideas, and the verb after each one takes the subjunctive.

lines: Il faut partir avant qu'il soit trop tard.
We need to leave before it's too late.
Je parle lentement pour que tu comprennes.
I speak slowly so that you understand.
Bien que je sois fatigué, je travaille.
Although I'm tired, I'm working.

parts.heading: Every phrase in one list
text: The verb after {que} takes the subjunctive after these phrases.

list: A need or a wish: {il faut que}, {je veux que}, {j'aimerais que}
A feeling: {je suis content que}, {je suis triste que}, {je suis désolé que}, {je suis surpris que}, {j'ai peur que}, {je regrette que}
A doubt: {je doute que}, {je ne pense pas que}, {je ne crois pas que}
A possibility: {il est possible que}, {il se peut que}
Time, purpose and contrast: {avant que}, {pour que}, {bien que}

checks.ask: Which one means “I want you to come”?
checks.why: A wish about someone else takes {que} and the subjunctive: {que tu viennes}.

checks.ask: After which phrase does the next verb change?
checks.why: {il faut que} states a need, so the verb after it takes the subjunctive. After {je pense que} and {peut-être que}, the verb stays as it is.

checks.ask: Which one means “I don't think he's coming”?

options.text: Je ne pense pas qu'il vienne.

checks.why: {je ne pense pas que} expresses a doubt, so the verb changes: {qu'il vienne}.
